children: By Aamir Khalid

Australian shares closed slightly lower on Tuesday, weighed by banks and technology stocks, as a fifth straight monthly fall in home prices and persistent inflation concerns dented sentiment ahead of key growth data.
Although the benchmark S&P/ASX 200
finished only marginally lower at 9,066.70 points, it had sunk as much as 0.6% intraday to a near two week low. The benchmark fell 0.2% on Monday.

The market had a tepid start to September as investors awaited the release of GDP data on Wednesday, which will provide clues to the economy's resilience and the Reserve Bank's future policy decisions.

"The ASX is starting September against a challenging macro backdrop, as rising global bond yields, oil above US$90 and renewed rate-hike concerns leave investors with fewer reasons to add risk," said Hebe Chen, a market analyst at Vantage Markets.
A fifth straight month of declines in Australian home prices in August further dampened the mood, marking the sharpest downturn since the pandemic and pressuring households and the broader economy.
In Sydney, banks
fell 0.4%, with the "Big Four" banks in the red except ANZ Group
, which was up 0.4%.

"With softer mortgage demand increasingly challenging the sector’s growth outlook, banks are now caught between a weaker housing market and renewed rate-hike risk, further exacerbating pressure on credit demand," added Chen.
Discretionary stocks (.AXDJ) and real estate stocks (.AXRE) slipped 1.8% and 0.1%, respectively.
Tech stocks
dropped 0.8%, tracking a fall in U.S. peer Nasdaq.
Bucking the trend, energy stocks
gained 1.2%, their best day since August 11, buoyed by rising crude prices.
Miners
rose 0.9%, as copper prices firmed, with mining giants BHP Group
and Rio Tinto
rising more than 0.9% each.
In New Zealand, the benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index
fell 0.9% to 13,786.90 points. Investors now turn to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's rate decision on Wednesday, with markets expecting a 25 basis point rate hike to 2.75%.
